concerns_addressed: Diff 2edf23e..246133c touches only the five OBJECTIVE files; no out-of-scope client, schema, dependency, or migration changes.
POST /tracker/items and canonical /work-items share createTrackerItemHandler via tracker-items router rewrite (tracker-items.ts:413, work-items.ts:19-25).
T7-C01, T7-S01, T7-S04, T7-S05, T7-S06, and T7-S07 integration scenarios are implemented in tracker-item-create-metadata.integration.test.ts and pass under RUN_INTEGRATION=1.
T7-S02 route parity and T7-S03 mocked regression scenarios pass in work-items.test.ts and tracker-items.write.test.ts.
Validation runs inside db.transaction via lockTaskCreateReferences + validateTaskCreateMetadata before counter/insert/relations/activity writes (tracker-item-create.ts:169-283).
Invalid metadata returns aggregated fieldErrors with HTTP 400 and no persisted rows; publishEvent is best-effort after commit with try/catch (tracker-item-create.ts:307-322).
Hydration queries execute inside the transaction before COMMIT per T7-S07 (hydrateCreatedItem at tracker-item-create.ts:241-273).
Conventional commit feat(tracker): create items with strict atomic metadata exists at reviewed SHA.

strengths: Clean extraction: tracker-items POST handler delegates to createTrackerItemHandler; ~170 lines of inline create logic removed from tracker-items.ts.
validateCreate / insertTrackerItem / hydrateCreatedItem separation keeps transaction flow readable without duplicating T3 validator or lock primitives.
legacyResponse preserves canonical vs legacy response shape by stripping source only on the legacy alias.
Integration suite uses real PostgreSQL with publisher spy only; unit suites retain mocked DB harness and document the pre- vs in-transaction validation shift.
All packet tests green: 6 integration + 23 unit tests in scoped files.
